accepted_findings: Marketplace GET Menu is scoped to an onboarding ID or store configured to the active provider, not a marketplace-wide feed.
Storefront exposes authenticated business/store-scoped menus with item identifiers and an original_image_url field.
Marketplace access is approval-only and the published integration pipeline is currently at capacity.
The sitemap proves broad geography only, not restaurant count, menu freshness, image population, rights, or coverage.
No public grant establishes SeeFood retention, display, matching, combination, or deletion rights.
required_corrections: Treat 168 DoorDash records as catalog-source Management classifications, not verified original merchant/POS authorship.
Separate menu and item-linkage schema from image-field population.
Call identifiers documented rather than stable because refresh stability was not measured.
Scope the capacity finding to Marketplace.
Allow direct merchant/POS authorization as an alternative to a DoorDash-originated grant for original controller payloads.

founder_scope_correction.instruction: Do not reject DoorDash scraping merely because the standard authorized API path fails.
founder_scope_correction.effect: The final record preserves scraping as a separate, potentially High technical hypothesis. Its live national probe remains gated by the current bot-control boundary or written consent.
